newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn gains extended amid weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn gains extended amid weather concerns.

text.p: Gains were extended in CBOT corn futures at midday amid concerns about forecasts for hotter, drier weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"There were no changes in the midday forecasts and funds have bought about 40 million bushels," said Mark Cermak, analyst for O'Connor and Co.
Cermak also said December corn moved above the 50-day moving average of $2.52-1/2 per bushel, which triggered buy stops.
Meteorologists Tuesday said a heat wave was expected in the Midwest through Friday. They said high temperatures would range from the low- to high-90-degrees-Fahrenheit area, beginning Tuesday.

Concerns were cited that the hot weather would harm some of the corn crop which is entering its crucial pollination stage. USDA Monday said seven percent of the U.S. corn crop was silking as of Sunday. Silking is the early stage of pollination.
At 1200 CDT, corn was four to eight cents per bushel higher, with July up 6-3/4 at $2.68-3/4 a bushel. September was up 7-1/4 at $2.55-3/4 and December was 7-3/4 cents higher at $2.56-3/4.
Also USDA Monday cited a deterioration in the condition of the U.S. crop. As of Sunday, USDA said, the crop was 73 percent good to excellent, below the 75 percent in that category the previous week.
